items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: We all played an Army transcription with the band. The guy's name was Earl Spencer.

ctx.x: This is where I first met Al Hibbler. He was living at the Silver Thong(?). And the great Al Killian, the trumpet player, had been doing some work for Norman Granz on the Jazz At The Philharmonic, and decided to stay out here.

I'd like to mention a thing that happened with Al Killian. We all played an Army transcription with the band. The guy's name was Earl Spencer. You remember he used to do the Army transcriptions, make these transcriptions for the Army to play in different parts of the world? And I'll never forget, during the recording Al Killian was sitting on the far end of the bandstand, and the piano was on the other side. And during one of those arrangements, he played a double high C, and the double high C on the piano just…
